errors.what: Round five's first calibration run crashed in its table printer (tally assumed every cell) after 13 min of fits; no threshold was read from it. Fixed the printer, committed, reran unchanged on the same seed.

The round-five worker first imported round four's eval module, whose top-level worker hook posted round four's verdicts; the smoke run showed all-zero one-tick counts. Moved the judge into its own worker file before any recorded run.

Full suite failed one test: update-rate-columns.test.mjs re-runs the 2026-11-12 rounding eval with the default catch-up and compares it to its file; under the Markov default 2/200 R1 walks became catch-ups (198 vs 200). Pinned that eval to catchUp {method: null} (it predates any catch-up), recorded the 2/200 in the README.

doc_friction.issue: Its unconditional `if (!isMainThread) parentPort.postMessage(...)` hook fires in any worker that imports the module for its CELLS, silently answering with round four's verdicts; later eval rounds must keep their worker entry in a separate file.
Re-ran an older eval under whatever CATCHUP was the default (763 s), so changing the default broke a historical-file test after a 16-minute suite run; now pinned.

notes: Pre-registered round five (commit 4cd7a9b45, before any recorded run): Markov carry-forward M1; tau 6.56 from null cells on calibration seed 31 (X1 binding); confirmation seed 20261217, 200 series a cell, 1619 s: K1-K5 pass, T3 96.8% (60/62) vs round four 80.6% (50/62) on the same series; R <= 1.0%, X1 1.5%, X2 0%; X3 (not judged) 81.5% vs 83.5%. Shipped as CATCHUP default. Local checks: rounded-walk-markov (5), rounded-walk-heavy (6), rounded-walk (5), update-rate-catchup (5), update-rate (7) pass; full venture suite via run_venture_tests.py, see PR.

pricing.source: Anthropic pricing as cached in the Claude API skill (models table and per-model migration notes), 2026-10-06. Cache writes are 1.25x input (5-minute) and 2x input (1-hour); cache reads differ by model.

human_equivalent.basis: a statistician designing, pre-registering, calibrating and running one simulation round with a new filter model, plus docs

certainty.tokens: high: summed from the per-request `usage` the API returned, as the transcript recorded it, deduplicated by message id
certainty.model: high: the `model` field on each API response, not the configured model
certainty.api_equivalent_usd: medium: measured tokens x list prices in prompts/pricing.json (as_of stated); an equivalent, not a charge: these runs are billed under a subscription
certainty.time: medium: from transcript timestamps; model time is request-to-response, tool time is call-to-result, time waiting on a person is excluded from active time
certainty.human_equivalent: low: the agent's own estimate of how long a competent person would take, with its basis written down; never measured

not_counted: requests the harness makes outside the transcript (context compaction summaries, title generation, safety classifiers), if any
transcripts lost when a cloud session moved to a new container: only files present in this container are read, so a resumed session can undercount
